# Changelog

## 0.1.4 (Windows candidate, unpublished)

Launcher-only Windows NTFS directory custody and writer locking replace the
previous non-POSIX no-op. Linux ownership/flock behavior is retained. All pinned
runtime modules/configurations and historical record bytes are unchanged.

## 0.1.3

The runtime closure, the replay-only amended runtime and the V1-V5
configurations are unchanged (`python3 -m headgasket pins --check`). The
launcher (`headgasket/cli.py`) changes:

- `serve`: a `remove` whose `route_id` is not one of the routes of an installed
  part that comes off on its own is answered by the launcher, with the part's
  routes, and is not passed to the pinned server, which would refuse it and then
  fail that call and every later one while scoring it (JSON-RPC error `-32602`).
  The call is not recorded and uses no attempt; `serve` prints how many there
  were when it stops. See `RELEASE-NOTES-0.1.3.md` in the repository root.
- `--version`, the start line and `launch.json` say 0.1.3; the MCP `serverInfo`
  version and `configs/PINS.json` still say 0.1.0 (pinned files).

## 0.1.2

The runtime closure, the replay-only amended runtime and the V1-V5
configurations are unchanged (`python3 -m headgasket pins --check`). The
launcher (`headgasket/cli.py`) changes:

- `serve`: a start that makes no tool call (a client's health check, a listed or
  restarted server) records nothing and leaves nothing in `--out`; what such a
  start left behind when it was killed is cleared at the next start; a lock keeps
  a second server out of a folder in use; a `--out` that is a link, holds links,
  holds other files, belongs to another user or can be written by other users is
  refused (a folder its group can write to is accepted); a new folder is created
  readable only by its owner; `launch.json` is written without following links,
  `0600`.
- `serve`: once the 1,024-attempt budget (or the tool-call guard) is spent, the
  launcher answers each further `tools/call` itself with the refusal the game
  gives (`Environment turn budget reached`, `turns_remaining` 0) and does not pass
  it to the pinned server, so the record stops at the budget and can be scored.
- `serve` refuses an interpreter other than CPython 3.12.
- `serve` reads its input as UTF-8 with invalid bytes turned into lone
  surrogates, so the pinned server answers them with a JSON-RPC error instead of
  stopping.
- `validate` says that it checks finished runs only and points to the
  repository validator for a run that stopped without `finish`.
- `--version`, the start line and `launch.json` say 0.1.2; the MCP `serverInfo`
  version and `configs/PINS.json` still say 0.1.0 (pinned files).

## 0.1.0

First public release of the environment. Runtime closure
`f347b0c8eee94ba36cd69818603178eb7e4c10e5afc4e21cf8eb8ec6308a4963`
(18 modules plus bootstrap, byte-identical to the sealed
`hardened-v6-aecadda` epoch), plus the replay-only amended runtime
`10967be0011b7c7808a47a108e74b1076f5141b10a5d5a7d39fa4d4087e8179b`
(`epochs/amended-v5/`, epoch `24a5713`). Adds the `headgasket` launcher
(serve, replay, verify, validate, prepare, family, pins, tools), the V1-V5
configurations (byte-identical to the configurations in the published run
records, and regenerated byte for byte by `prepare`), the test suite and the
documentation. See `docs/PROVENANCE.md` for what differs from the sealed epoch
and why.
